A.explanation: Point Q is near where the graph starts to curve, but the elastic limit cannot be fixed from a loading curve alone without unloading to check for permanent extension.

B.explanation: Point R is already on the curved section, while the limit of proportionality is where the initial straight line from the origin ends.

C.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit some work is dissipated as heat and permanent deformation, so the total area is not all stored as recoverable elastic potential energy.

D.explanation: For any stretching, small work $dW = Fdx$ sums to the area under the force-extension curve from P to S.

hints: Look at the shape of the force-extension curve from the origin through Q and R to S and find where it stops being a straight line.
Recall that work done in stretching is $W = \int F dx$, which is the area under the force against extension graph.
Think about why total work done and stored elastic potential energy are the same only up to the elastic limit, and differ once permanent stretching occurs.
walkthrough: Identify the axes: vertical force $F$ against horizontal extension $x$ for loading from the origin at P to S, with an initial straight section then a curve through Q and R.
State the proportionality rule: $F = kx$ while the graph is straight, so the limit of proportionality is at the end of the straight section, before the obvious curve.

Note that Q and R are both marked on or near the curved part, and the elastic limit needs an unloading test for permanent set, so neither point can be identified as a limit with certainty from this graph alone.
State the energy rule: for a small stretch $dx$, work $dW = Fdx$, so total work $W = \int F dx$ is the area under the graph from P to S in $\text{J}$.
Distinguish work from stored energy: up to the elastic limit all work is stored as elastic potential energy, but beyond it part is lost to plastic deformation and heat.
Therefore the area must always equal work done, but must equal stored elastic potential energy only if the wire stayed elastic. This is option D.
